findings.evidence: template/scripts/lifecycle_workers.py:335-336 (provider_readiness) builds `clean = credential_free_env(dict(os.environ), scratch_home(...))` and uses it for every provider's `runner.preflight`; it never calls `llm_env`. main() (lines ~829-838) uses this readiness to compute `review_ready`, and `job_eligible` filters jobs on it. With CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN now stripped from credential_free_env and no token injected here, the claude model probe on macOS cannot authenticate even when `[independent_review.login.claude] token_file` is valid. This contradicts the proposal's success criterion (a claude review job runs with a valid token_file) and the 'declared token reaches the provider's LLM environment' requirement. Only independent_review.py preflight (`bound_preflight`) was changed to use the bound env.
findings.summary: The worker's startup provider readiness probe still runs the claude model probe in a credential-free env without the declared token, so a bound claude login can still be reported not ready and its review jobs filtered out before the new login preflight runs.
